But if he looks only at what God has made lawful for him to look at, and takes himself to account over the glance; and speaks only with what God has made lawful for him, and takes his tongue to account over speech; and hears only what God has made lawful for him to hear, and takes his hearing to account over what he hears; and thinks only about what God has made lawful for him to think about, and takes his intellect to account over that thinking; and so on in all his limbs — this is the one whose limbs will become upright for him and whose soul will be driven along behind the command of God, glorified and exalted.

This soul, for all its faults, if it is trained accepts training, and if it is raised accepts upbringing. There is no soul but that in it are many elements of good that can be built upon. Among the greatest of these elements is the innate constitution (fiṭrah) upon which God constituted it. For God constituted all people upon His oneness and upon acknowledging His lordship and His divinity, and constituted them all upon fear of Him and hope in Him, and constituted them all upon desire for what is with Him. This original constitution is among the most important elements relied upon in the upbringing of the soul.

Then after that, what the soul learns of the revelation is an important element in straightening it and raising it, because this revelation coming from outside the soul, from God, glorified and exalted, directs the soul to the positions it cannot arrive at by thinking and by intellect. Every place the intellect cannot reach and cannot attach itself to — its exposition comes in the revelation.

Then after that the third element is the intellect, by which a person grasps his benefits and his harms. For there is no doubt that a person who believes in the Garden and the Fire desires the Garden and fears the Fire; and there is no doubt that a person who knows he will be held to account and recompensed, and that he has two scale-pans on the Day of Resurrection, desires that the pan of good deeds outweigh; and there is no doubt that a person who believes that the companion of the right and the companion of the left are with him, writing all that he utters and all that he does, desires the increase of his good deeds and the decrease of his evil deeds. This is what the intellect requires in the first place; and if he does not act according to what it requires, this intellect becomes a proof against him and not for him.

Then this taking of account also requires of a person the severing of heedlessness. For among what makes a person need to take account are the lapses of heedlessness that come upon him. A human being is much given to forgetfulness and much given to sleep and heedlessness, and his abundant and successive preoccupations hold him back from many of his works. So he needs, at intervals and from time to time, to review these lapses of heedlessness so as not to be driven along behind a matter he is convinced is an annihilating harm to him.

Surges of appetite come upon a person, and there also comes upon him an original ignorance in him, so that he is ignorant of his own benefit, or rides his appetite while knowing that it is a harm to him. But if he remembers, he returns, as God, exalted be He, said: {Truly those who are God-conscious, when a visitation from Satan touches them, they remember, and at once they see. And their brethren draw them on into error, then they do not stop short} (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:201-202). So those who are God-conscious may be made to slip by Satan because of some of what they have earned, but they do not persist in his making them slip; rather they quickly remember God, glorified and exalted, and His watching, and so they return to Him and repent: {Truly those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met — Satan only made them slip because of some of what they had earned; and God has pardoned them} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:155).

For that reason, when many calamities surround a person and the cares of this world press dark upon his face, he needs to appoint for himself an hour of rest; and it can only be by taking account.

This taking of account is what makes it possible to straighten one's work. Abraham, peace be upon him, when he was building the Kaaba, whenever he raised the building would come down and look at it so as to see its straightness. Ibn al-Jawzi, may God have mercy on him, said: "Among the elect are a people who, since they awoke, have not slept, and since they set out, have not halted; whenever they covered a stretch they looked and saw the deficiency of what they were in, and so they sought forgiveness." Those people travel upon the road of guidance, and since they came to know the road of guidance they have kept to it and not left it and not halted upon it for a moment; they continue upon this road, but whenever they cover a stretch they look and grasp the deficiency of what they were in, and so they seek forgiveness and repent to God, glorified and exalted, from that deficiency — and by this they continue forward in their work. For a person's whole march requires of him continuation and perseverance upon the road of truth.

Then God, glorified and exalted, has aided us with external elements, besides these internal elements, in taking account of the soul and watching over it. Among the most important of these elements is the awareness of the presence of the noble angels: {And truly over you are keepers, noble writers, who know what you do} (Sūrat al-Infiṭār 82:10-12); {He utters no word but that with him is a watcher ready} (Sūrat Qāf 50:18); {For him are successive angels before him and behind him, guarding him by God's command} (Sūrat al-Raʿd 13:11). These noble angels do not disobey God in what He commands them and do what they are commanded; and they surround a person from his right and his left and before him: on his right and his left the two writers, and before him the successive ones "before him and behind him" — before him and behind him likewise.

So a person's awareness of these witnessing angels, and of the writing of what they write, and that he will be given that record and will come carrying it on his neck — {And every human being We have fastened his omen to his neck, and We shall bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will meet spread open. Read your record! Sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:13-14) — this requires of a person that he take himself to account before that reckoning: take account of yourselves before you are taken to account, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed.

Then after this, the watching of the Watcher, the Witness. For a person must grasp that God, glorified and exalted, is aware of his states: no heaven veils another heaven from Him, nor any earth another earth, nor any mountain what is in its rugged places, nor any sea what is in its depth: {And We are nearer to him than the jugular vein} (Sūrat Qāf 50:16).

God, glorified and exalted, will spread His shelter over His believing servant on the Day of Resurrection and will say: "O My servant, do you remember the day when you did such-and-such, and I had forbidden you from it?" And he will say: "My Lord, I remember it, and I had forgotten it." And He will say: "But I did not forget it." And this is along with His concealing him and His spreading His shelter over him, glorified be He — how forbearing and generous He is!

As for the enemies of God, glorified and exalted, and the depraved who do not care, God will expose them before the heads of the witnesses and establish the proof against them. A banner will be set up for every treacherous one at his backside on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be proclaimed over him before the heads of the witnesses: "This is the treachery of so-and-so the son of so-and-so." A person would not accept disgrace before an assembly of the people of this world, however small that assembly, so how could he accept disgrace in the Highest Assembly, before the Judge, with the witness of the angels brought near and the prophets and the righteous and all creatures? It is the greatest disgrace, after which there is no disgrace.

For that reason a person must take himself to account now and must remember this divine watching: "for if you do not see Him, He sees you."

Then after this, a person must grasp also that God has witnesses from his own self. These limbs will testify against people for what they have committed: {On the day when their tongues and their hands and their feet testify against them for what they used to do — on that day God will pay them their due recompense in full, and they will know that God is the manifest Truth} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:24-25). For if a human being were a single block, it would have been possible that no part of him should testify against another, or that this should not be conceivable. But God made him branches and extremities, and made them witnesses against him, when He seals his tongue and his limbs speak: his hair and his skin speak, and his two hands and his two feet; every limb speaks of what it committed. For when a person remembers that scene he tries to bend his limbs back so that they will not be among the witnesses against him on the Day of Resurrection.

Then among these external means likewise is the testimony of people, for people are God's witnesses. That is why the Messenger of God (ṣ) said, when a funeral bier was carried past him and the people praised the dead one with good, "It is due"; then another passed and the people spoke ill of it, and he said, "It is due." Umar said: "And what is due?" He said: "You are God's witnesses upon His earth. Whomever you praise with good, the Garden is due to him; and whomever you speak ill of, the Fire is due to him." So people are God's witnesses; and for that God, exalted be He, said: {And say: work, for God will see your work, and His Messenger and the believers} (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:105). So the testimony of people must be given its weight.

The greatest of witnesses among people is the Messenger of God (ṣ): for the deeds of his community are laid before him in his grave, so he is gladdened by their good and grieved by their evil, and he will testify against them on the Day of Resurrection: {So how will it be when We bring from every community a witness and bring you as a witness against these? On that day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were levelled over them, and they will not conceal from God any account} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:41-42). So if you stand in awe of the great and the eminent, is it not fitting that you should stand in awe of the Messenger of God (ṣ), before whom your deeds are laid? Is it not fitting that you should stand in awe of God's witnesses upon the earth, who testify to all your deeds?

Then after that, among the witnesses are this earth and this heaven, and they are among the external factors that assist in watching over the soul. For this earth clamours to God over the evil deeds upon it, and this heaven likewise testifies to the evil deeds done beneath its surface; and the fish in the water, and the creatures, and the plants — all of that is affected by evil deeds. Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people's hands have earned, so that He may make them taste some of what they have done, that perhaps they may return (cf. Sūrat al-Rūm 30:41). All of that is among God's witnesses, glorified and exalted.

Then among these external factors are the hours of time. For every hour that passes over you is a complete lifetime; and when that lifetime has elapsed its deeds are sealed up and are not unrolled except at the presentation before God. And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord, He says: "Is this not the truth?" They say: "Yes, by our Lord" (cf. Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:30) — on that day you will be presented, no hidden thing of yours will be hidden (cf. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah 69:18). Every hour that passes over us in this world is a complete lifetime whose work is sealed and whose pages are deposited. That is why angels come upon us in succession by night and angels by day, as is established as sound from the Prophet (ṣ): "Angels by night and angels by day come upon you in succession." So these angels testify, and God suffices as a witness; they raise the reports to God, glorified be He, of the deeds of the servants. And these reports are preserved and cannot be subject to alteration or change, except what God forgives of evil deeds and overlooks of faults; for He is the Forbearing, the Wise, the Generous, who forgives what He wills except associating partners with Him, glorified be He.

Then among the external factors likewise that assist in watching over and following up the soul is what befalls a person of illnesses and reminders and lessons. For if a person were, from the day he was born until his lifetime ended, in good health, and no fever nor headache befell him, and he complained of no pain and was not harmed by any harm, he might be heedless. But these afflictions — if this one misses him, that one strikes him, and they surround him on every side; so if you do not fall ill today with this illness, you are exposed to another illness — all of that by God's governance and His decree.

For this, my brother, you must grasp that every affliction among the afflictions of this world and every illness that strikes you is an alerting from God to you. This alerting is like the completion of faith. For when you pray the prayer as we have just prayed, and you have entered and stood before the Sovereign, the Judge, confiding in Him and praising Him and laying your needs before Him and exposing yourself to the good that is with Him — perhaps your mind wanders and perhaps you become heedless; then when that pillar of the prayer ends, the imam raises his voice: "God is greatest", and so you review yourself and return to yourself after you had wandered and gone right or left. Then you begin a new pillar containing a firm address other than the previous address; and if your soul wanders or your humility or your presence leaves you, the imam says "God is greatest", also as an alerting, and so the soul returns — and so on until the prayer ends. The imam raises his voice with every magnification and with every "God hears the one who praises Him" and with the salutation, so as to alert those present and bring them back to confiding in God, glorified and exalted, and to remind them of the majesty of the One they are confiding in; for they are confiding in the Sovereign, the Judge, glorified and exalted.

These many reminders that remind you of the departure from this abode: among the greatest of the external ones is death, which is the master of preachers, and death suffices as a preacher. For that reason, when you remember death and decay and your departure from this abode, and what people say behind your back — do they praise you with good or with ill? — and what they testify against you, and with what you will be mentioned in the Highest Assembly and with what you will be praised in the lowest assembly: all of that requires of you that you concern yourself with your own condition, and that you know that the grave before you is the first of the stations of the hereafter. When the son of Adam dies his resurrection has already come.

The first thing he meets in it is the squeezing of the grave, from which the ribs are dislocated and by which the shoulder-straps are removed. Then after that, the questioning of the two angels who seat a person in his grave and say: "Who is your Lord, and what is your religion, and what did you use to say about this man?" As for the believer, he says: "My Lord is God, and my religion is Islam, and the man raised among us is Muhammad (ṣ)" — he is Muhammad, he is Muhammad, he is Muhammad, three times — "he came to us with the clear proofs and the guidance, so we believed and followed." As for the hypocrite or the doubter — I do not know which of the two Asma said — he says: "Ah, ah, I do not know. I heard people saying something and I said it." How far apart are these two answers!

Then after that, if he was a true, affirming believer they say to him: "You have spoken truly and done well; sleep the sleep of a bride", and they fill his grave for him with greenery and light. As for the hypocrite or the doubter, they say to him: "You did not know and you did not follow", and they strike him with a sledgehammer they have with them such that, were the people of Mina to gather upon it, they could not lift it. And in the hadith of Asma: "and they strike him with hammers between his two temples, and he gives a cry heard by all who are near him except human beings and jinn."

So when a person grasps his own departure — and that perhaps their appointed term has drawn near — while believing in this departure and knowing that even if he lived the lifetime of Noah, death must come after that, and that this death is an inevitable destination unavoidable for all people, in which chiefs and subjects, the great and the small, are equal:

"Death does not despise the small one and so turn // aside from him, nor is the greatness of the great one awe-inspiring to it."
"And whoever does not die by the sword dies by something else; // the causes are many and death is one."
"It is death, from which there is no refuge and no escape: // when it sets this one down from his bier, that one mounts."

— then all are travelling upon this road, setting out towards it in earnest, striving in their work, racing towards death. This time which a person loves to have more of, and thinks about the coming month and the coming week and the coming day — all of that is a drawing near to the appointed term and a hastening at a trot towards the abode of the hereafter and towards the departure from this world. This death, the preacher, awaits us all, and we do not know who is tomorrow's delegation nor who is the delegation of the day after; but we are certain that we are all travelling to what lies there, as Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: "There is a watering place there that is come to, without any lie; // one must come to it one day just as they came to it."

That must be an aid to a person in taking account; and the one certain of this death, and certain of the grave and what is beyond it, must be prepared for it and ready for it. That is why one of those who attended a sermon of the Messenger of God (ṣ) said: "Are you in earnest that you did not witness the counsel of Muhammad, // the Messenger of the God, when he counselled and called to witness? // If you do not travel with a provision of God-consciousness, // and after death you meet one who did provide himself, // you will regret that you were not like him, // and that you did not make ready for the death he had made ready for."

All these factors are an aid to a person in taking account of himself, particularly if he reviews their particulars. For when you put on a garment that God has favoured you with and remember the remembrance transmitted concerning the putting on of a garment, and you say: "Praise belongs to God who has clothed me with what I cover my nakedness with and adorn myself with in my life" — you ought to make of it a witness over yourself and a watcher over it, so that you do not disobey God while wearing this garment with which He clothed you.

And when you sit in any gathering whatever, while you are in well-being in your body and in security in your dwelling, complaining of no abasement and no humiliation, you must remember that this blessing may not lawfully be spent in what does not please God, mighty and majestic; and that will be a summons from you to complete watching and taking account.

When you lie down upon your bed at the time of sleep and close your eyes after having remembered God and sealed with good, you remember that you are now coming upon a death from which you do not know whether you will rise from this lying-down or will not rise, and you take account of yourself over twenty-four hours that have passed. Then when the warner breaks forth and the dawn rises, you remember that you have entered a new covenant and a lifetime other than the previous lifetime, and that another chance at deliverance has been made available to you which may not be repeated — as al-Mawardi, may God have mercy on him, said: "Turn to your five prayers: // how many a one who reaches morning, and perhaps he will not reach evening. // And receive the new day with a repentance // that erases the sins of yesterday's page. // For decay will surely do to your fresh face // what darkness does to the image of the sun."

My brother, if you make this taking of account one of your concerns and your business, much of the commitment you demand of yourself will become easy for you. Many people complain that they resolve to continue in commitment, but their resolves are soon torn and weakened and they return to what does not please God. And many people make a covenant with God to commit to what pleases Him on occasions such as Ramadan and others, but they soon forget that covenant and go back on it. The cause is the neglect of watching and taking account.

But if this taking of account is present in the mind, then when a person remembers a power among his powers he says: "My Lord, by what You have favoured me with, I shall never be a supporter of the criminals" (cf. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:17). If he remembers any blessing among God's blessings, he remembers where it came from.

And you know that people regarding blessings are of four categories. A category who do not know a blessing by its presence but only know it by its departure: so long as one of them does not complain of a cancer in his liver, and does not complain of a failing in his heart or his kidneys, and does not complain of any pain in his tooth or his ear or his eye, he does not feel this blessing. But when the illness comes and he is held in the ward upon a hospital bed, he remembers the well-being he was in — and the time has passed; he was not going to exploit it or make use of it, and it has gone. And if he has wealth and family, he does not remember this blessing until it departs; so when his wealth is swept away or his family is taken from him and what he was enjoying, he remembers the state he was in and regrets where regret does not benefit. This kind of people are the people of loss, because the blessings were a proof against them and not for them, for they did not know them at all by their presence but only sensed them by their departure.

The second category of people are those who know a blessing by its presence but do not know where it came from. They know that they have been favoured over others, that they have knowledge and wealth and standing and strength and culture and office and position, but they do not know where it came from, and so they are heedless of thanking for it; and so it becomes a regret against them and a ruin. These are the likes of Qarun, who said: {It was only given to me because of knowledge I have}. Did he not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him in power and greater in accumulation? And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins (Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:78). Those people suppose that what is in their hands is only from their own earning and toil and striving, and this is the utmost in misguidance and deviation, as the poet said: "She spent the night reproaching me with poverty and destitution, // when she saw for her brother wealth and blessings. // Ruin take your opinion! Provisions are not from strength // nor from earning, but are apportioned in shares." So all of it is from God's apportioning, glorified and exalted, and His governance.

The third kind of people are those who know a blessing by its presence and know where it came from and that it is from God, but do not thank for it; rather they are distracted by the blessing from thanking for it. They are distracted by managing wealth and increasing it and putting it in order, and by caring for the body, its cleanliness and its perfume and its oiling, and by caring for the family, and by caring for everything they are in of blessings — distracted from thanking for those blessings. This is what God warned against in His Book,
saying: {O you who believe, let not your wealth nor your children distract you from the remembrance of God; and whoever does that, those are the losers. And spend of what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says: My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term, so that I might give charity and be among the righteous. But God will never delay a soul when its term has come; and God is aware of what you do} (Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn 63:9-11). And God reproached the desert Arabs for their preoccupation with that, saying: {Those of the desert Arabs who remained behind will say to you: our wealth and our families kept us busy} (Sūrat al-Fatḥ 48:11). These knew the blessing by its presence and knew that it is from God, but the blessing distracted them from the worship of God.

For this reason these blessings are one of the five fronts opened against a person, as we shall make clear after completing the fourth kind of people regarding blessings — and they are those who know a blessing by its presence and know that it is from God and are not distracted by the blessing from thanking for it, but rather expend it in what God is pleased with and in thanking Him. These are the fewest of God's servants: "and few of My servants are thankful" (cf. Sūrat Sabaʾ 34:13). Few are the people who expend their time in what they were created for and expend their strength in what they were created for, and who say truthfully: {Say: truly my prayer and my rites of sacrifice and my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds; He has no partner; and with that I have been commanded} (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:162-163). Few are the people who are truthful when they say that and call God to witness over it; "and few of My servants are thankful."

A person has had five fronts opened against him in this worldly life, and he is in need of elements of strengthening to strengthen him in the face of these five fronts.

The first front is Satan: {Truly Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy} (Sūrat Fāṭir 35:6).

The second front is evil companions, who turn a person away from obedience to God and occupy him with what does not concern him, and who are his enemies on the Day of Resurrection: {Friends on that day will be enemies to one another, except the God-conscious} (Sūrat al-Zukhruf 43:67); {And on the day when the wrongdoer bites his hands, saying: would that I had taken a way with the Messenger! Woe to me, would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend! He led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me; and Satan is ever a deserter of the human being} (Sūrat al-Furqān 25:27-29).

The third front is the soul that commands to evil.

The fourth front is God's blessings upon a person: if he does not expend them in thanksgiving, they are a front opened against him, as God, exalted be He, said: {O you who believe, truly among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. And if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then God is Forgiving, Merciful. Your wealth and your children are only a trial} (Sūrat al-Taghābun 64:14-15).

The fifth front is this world, for it is the abode of delusion, and it is the co-wife of the hereafter, distracting from it. For this a person must be alert to this abode so that it does not delude him. It is not an abode of remaining nor an abode of continuance; rather it is a flowing show, and the continuance of a state is impossible. Everything in it passes away, and everything raised up in it will become lowly: it was a right upon God that He raise nothing of this world but that He lower it.

The most important thing people compete over and the dearest of the matters of this world will after a short while become dust thrown into the rubbish. For the luxurious cars on which people expend vast sums, and the costly clothes over which people outbid one another, and the kinds of precious goods people compete over — what is their destination after their use? Will they not be thrown into the rubbish, and will a person not be repelled at the sight of them? This is the state of the whole of this world.

Even a human being: when he dies, the dearest and nearest of people to him is the one who hastens to prepare him and bury him in the earth. If anything of this world were continuing, a person after death would be beloved to his family and they would not bury him, but would leave him with them in his house upon his bed. Would anyone accept to leave his dead relative upon his bed with him in his house until his bones scattered? No one would accept this; rather it is the utmost for a human being in abasement and humiliation — because God favoured him by causing him to die and then giving him a grave, that is, making him of those who are buried.

All of this indicates to us that this world is not an abode of settlement. That is why the kings of old used to write in their councils: "Had it lasted for another than you, it would not have reached you" — "had it lasted for another than you, it would not have reached you." Had kingship endured, it would not have reached you, O king, or O president who sits upon the chair; for presidents and kings have sat upon this chair before, and the dominions have passed from hand to hand, and you have taken it for a period whose length you do not know, and you will depart and leave it to those after you. So this requires of you that you take account.

A person, when he occupies any office — whether official or social or an ordinary job — must remember that his occupying that office is like his sitting upon the barber's chair for his head to be shaved; then he will rise from it and leave it to those after him. He can neither advance nor delay when the messengers of God come to him: when it is said to him "Come to the hereafter", he cannot refuse, nor take a decision, nor gather the parliament or the government so as to take a decision by consultation in the matter: {When their term comes they cannot delay an hour nor advance it} (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:34).

For that reason a person must make ready for this decreed term, and must take himself to this account over both the weighty matters and the small ones. Many people can take themselves to account over the weighty matters but are heedless of the small ones, and this is the state that happens to many people: they suppose themselves to be upon good so long as they have avoided falling into much of what people fall into. But these have fallen into another great matter, which is being deluded about God and feeling safe from His devising. The one who falls into an act of disobedience, even a small one, must fear — because he has been negligent towards God and has contravened His command and fallen into what He forbade him, even if that act of disobedience was small.

Therefore when a person looks at others, his look at them must not be with the aim of taking them to account; for he is not responsible for taking people to account, but is responsible for taking himself to account. Malik brought out in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, and Ahmad in al-Zuhd, from Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Ansari, that it reached him that Jesus son of Mary used to say: "Do not speak much other than in the remembrance of God, lest your hearts harden; for the hard heart is far from God, but you do not know. And do not look into the sins of people as though you were lords, but look into your own sins as though you were slaves. People are only the afflicted and the spared: so have mercy on the people of affliction and praise God for well-being."

So a person must not be occupied with taking others to account instead of taking himself to account. The small matters are the root of the great ones: a person may fall into a small sin, but through it he grows bold towards God, and so that small one calls him to a great one — we ask God for safety and well-being. And there are the evil deeds of recompense: many people's evil deeds cast them down into other evil deeds which are of the kind of recompense, because they are driven off; and the driving-off with which God drives them off is that He makes easy for them what is harmful to them of evil deeds — we ask God for safety and well-being.

Then among the taking of account is also what requires that a person review his speech. For a single word of God's good pleasure raises a person degrees in the Garden, and a single word of God's wrath casts a person down seventy autumns into the bottom of Hell. For that reason a person must strive in this taking of account.

Then there is another kind, no less important than what has preceded of taking account, and it is the taking of account by the people of righteousness of themselves. What we have been speaking of is taking account for what a person falls into of disobedience to God and what he is negligent in towards God. But we must also take account of ourselves over the acts of obedience to God, and over doing them well and perfecting them.

This prayer which we pray — we must set for it a plan of follow-up and taking account. Does our prayer forbid us from indecency and wrong? Is our prayer really at the required level? Is it really in accordance with how we saw the Messenger of God (ṣ) pray? Does it expiate evil deeds? {Truly the prayer forbids indecency and wrong; and the remembrance of God is greater; and God knows what you make} (Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:45). The Prophet (ṣ) made clear that the prayer expiates what is below the ruinous major sins; but not every prayer is like that — rather what is meant by it is the sound (ṣaḥīḥ) prayer, in accordance with what was legislated and in accordance with what the Messenger of God (ṣ) made clear.

Likewise the taking of account in every work a person presents to God, glorified and exalted. For God, exalted be He, said: {And those who give what they give while their hearts are quaking that they are returning to their Lord — those hasten in good works and they are foremost in them} (Sūrat al-Muʾminūn 23:60-61). And it is established as sound from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she asked the Messenger of God (ṣ) about this verse: is it the one who commits the indecency while hating it and being fearful and afraid? He said: "No, rather it is the one who prays and gives charity and fasts while fearing that God will not accept it from him" — "and those who give what they give while their hearts are quaking that they are returning to their Lord."

So this quaking is indispensable, and it is what many people lack. Many Muslims, and many of their common folk, truly rejoice in obedience, but they rely upon it in many cases; while the Prophet (ṣ) says: "Not one of you will enter the Garden by his work." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God should envelop me in His mercy."

We are in need of reviewing our whole work. Prayer very often turns into a habit which a person performs because he found his grandfathers and his fathers practising it, and so he becomes accustomed to what they accustomed him to; and he practises all the works without thinking about their cause. He gathers wealth without knowing why he gathers it; he makes the pilgrimage as he saw people making the pilgrimage; he fasts as he saw them fasting; he gives charity as he saw them giving charity — without that springing from his own faith and proceeding from his own conviction.

Likewise in calling to God: for calling very often turns into a hobby among hobbies, which a person practises with the spirit of a hobbyist, as the sportsman practises sport and as the owner of a hobby of collecting postage stamps or coins practises his hobby. So he gives lectures and takes part in calling and attends it merely as a hobby, without intending by that to draw near to God, glorified and exalted. How many works like mountains have gone as scattered dust when sincerity did not accompany them and the truthful intention did not accompany them! And how many long sittings in times of heat and hardship, and works neglected, which could have been heavy in the pan of good deeds on the Day of Resurrection — but they were lost and went, because a person did not attend them with the spirit of worship and did not turn in them to God and was not sincere to Him.

The truthful person, when he takes steps to the mosque from the beginning of his house, makes an intention for every step: the step that expiates an evil deed and the step that raises a good deed — all of that with intention and purpose. And when he sits in the mosque he intends the being-a-neighbour and the sitting with those who worship God in the place honoured with God, in houses which God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered. And when he speaks a word of God's good pleasure he intends by it the face of God, and is not like those with whom the Fire will be kindled on the Day of Resurrection.

For the Messenger of God (ṣ) mentioned a number of men who are the first with whom the Fire will be kindled on the Day of Resurrection. A man whom God taught knowledge and who occupied himself with teaching it; so He called him and made known to him His blessing upon him and he acknowledged it, and He said: "And what did you do in it?" He said: "I taught knowledge for Your sake." God said: "You have lied", and the angels said: "You have lied. You only taught so that it would be said: a scholar — and it has been said." So the command is given concerning him and he is dragged upon his face and thrown into the Fire. And a man to whom God gave of the kinds of wealth what He gave, and he spent it; so He made known to him His blessing upon him and he acknowledged it, and He said: "And what did you do in it?" He said: "My Lord, I left no avenue in which You love wealth to be spent but that I spent in it." God says: "You have lied", and the angels say: "You have lied. You only spent so that it would be said: generous — and it has been said." And a man who fought until he was killed; so God makes known to him His blessing upon him and he acknowledges it, and He says: "And what did you do in it?" He says: "My Lord, I strove in Your way until I was killed." God says: "You have lied", and the angels say: "You have lied. You only fought so that it would be said: brave — and it has been said." So the command is given concerning him and he is dragged upon his face and thrown into the Fire. We ask God for safety and well-being.

The importance of taking account from this angle is that it requires sincerity. And if a person does not remember the intention at the beginning of a work, he must make it sincere in the middle of it — as with the whole lifetime. It has been transmitted from al-Hasan al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, that he said: "A lifetime whose beginning was squandered is well worth having its end preserved." So what has been lost of one's lifetime and gone — if you regret it and grieve over it, do not let your portion of that be regret and anguish; rather try, my brother, to do well in the future. For if there remained of your lifetime only a forearm's length and you did well in it, it would settle the account of all that has passed.

Those who complain of the evil deeds that have piled up and of conduct that was not pleasing, and who blame themselves for what has passed — the opportunity is open before them to repent and turn back and do well. God, glorified and exalted, calls us with His generous call and says: "Say: O My servants who have been excessive against themselves, do not despair of God's mercy; truly God forgives all sins; truly He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you and then you are not helped. And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive — lest a soul should say: alas for my negligence towards God, and I was indeed among the mockers; or it should say: had God guided me I would have been among the God-conscious; or it should say, when it sees the punishment: if only I had another turn, that I might be among the doers of good" — and "the turn" is the return, that is: if only I had a return to this world after death, that I might be among the doers of good — "Yes indeed, My signs came to you and you denied them and were arrogant and were among the disbelievers. And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against God, their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a lodging for the arrogant? And God will deliver those who were God-conscious by their attainment: no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve} (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:53-61).

May God bless me and you in the Mighty Qur'an and benefit me and you by what is in it of signs and the wise Reminder; and may He turn in forgiveness to me and to you, for He is the Ever-Relenting, the Merciful. I say this my saying and I ask God's forgiveness for me and for you; and may God bless and grant peace to our Prophet Muhammad and to his family and all his Companions.

I think it is better that the questions be kept for tomorrow, God willing — Thursday, in the neighbouring mosque, the Mosque of Remembrance — because I have fatigue and illness now and am not able to continue.

This is a complete lecture/sermon transcript delivered after a prayer — the Sheikh refers to 'the prayer as we have just prayed' and, in the passage on the oath by the sun, to the afternoon timing — and it closes with the standard sermon formula before he defers questions to the next day.

This record uses '(ص)' throughout as an abbreviation for the prayer upon the Prophet, as IDs 478, 481, 486 and 491 do. The English expands it to '(ṣ)'; body_ar preserves the abbreviation as published.

The lecture's structure should be visible in any display, because the argument is cumulative and is not a list of exhortations. It runs: (1) the eleven oaths of Sūrat al-Shams, taken one by one, as a proof of the weight God attaches to the purification of the soul; (2) the two senses of tazkiyah — cleansing (taṭhīr) and growth (namāʾ) — and therefore the two operations of divesting (takhliyah) and adorning (taḥliyah); (3) the four-part programme of the Muslim's life — knowledge, action, calling, patience — derived twice over, from Sūrat al-ʿAṣr and from Luqman's counsel, and yielding certainty plus patience equals leadership in religion; (4) the internal aids to self-accounting (fiṭrah, revelation, intellect); (5) the external aids (the recording angels, the divine watching, the limbs as witnesses, people as God's witnesses, the earth and sky, the hours, illness, the prayer's own takbīrs, and death and the grave); (6) the four categories of people with respect to blessings; (7) the five open fronts (Satan, evil companions, the commanding soul, unthanked blessings, this world); and (8) self-accounting over acts of obedience themselves, which is the sincerity argument, ending on the hadith of the first three cast into the Fire and on al-Hasan al-Basri's word about redeeming the end of a life.

CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. Two passages invert if excerpted. First, the four categories of people regarding blessings only make sense as a set of four: the fourth (those who know the blessing, know its source, and spend it in thanks) is the point, and each of the first three is described as a failure mode, not as a position being commended. Second, the hadith of the first three cast into the Fire concerns the scholar, the spender and the fighter; lifted out of the sincerity argument it reads as a condemnation of teaching, giving and fighting as such, which is the opposite of the lecture's claim — the Sheikh has just spent the lecture commanding all three.

The distinction between hidāyat al-irshād (the guidance of direction, which is affirmed of the Prophet at Sūrat al-Shūrā 42:52) and hidāyat al-tawfīq (the guidance of enabling-success, whose power is denied him at Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:56) is the theological hinge of the first third of the lecture, and the English keeps both terms distinct and glossed throughout rather than collapsing both into 'guidance'.

EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED, on two counts, neither of them doctrinal: the factual claim about the sun's surface temperature, which style guide 11 requires be preserved rather than corrected, and the passage addressing kings and presidents. Both are flagged. Nothing in the record has been softened.
